messages:
sasha: heads up — after the 2.1.0 kernel-routing tweak we started seeing intermittent OOMs on paged-attn workloads. repro rate ~4% on nightly cluster. attaching quick dump.
kevin: saw this too. allocation heatmap shows a cluster of small free holes that never get reused — looks like 'ghost' blocks sitting around. low-level trace attached.
maria: ghost blocks = leftover slab fragments, right? thought compaction would reclaim them.
kevin: yup. compaction runs, but the compaction cost is spiking CPU and adding ~8–12ms tail on generation. when compaction is delayed, reuse rate drops and GPU WS fills.
jordan: basic hypothesis: the recent kernel fanout change altered lifetime distribution (short-lived allocations now take chunk path vs slab), so small-block churn increased fragmentation.

sasha: exact. micro-benchmark comparing slab vs chunk pathways:
```
alloc pattern: 128B x 480k reqs over 120s
slab reuse: 72% -> 85% after bump
chunk reuse: 18% -> 9% (post-change)
compaction runs per min: 3 -> 9
mean compaction pause: 3.2ms -> 9.1ms
```
kevin: interestingly, KV-cache lookups spike during compaction leading to wasted KV cache fill and more background allocations.

tara: can we try two quick experiments:
- 1) force small-blocks to slab path for a day (config flag)
- 2) reduce compaction aggressiveness but add periodic eager coalesce during low-latency windows

maria: i prototyped config for (1). set slab_bucket_scale=1.18 and slab_prio_threshold=0.32. also disabled chunk_promote_for_shortlived=true. patch posted to playbook.

sasha: rolled experiment to canary group (10% traffic) 10:30 PDT. initial telemetry (10m): OOMs -> 0; but 95p latency increased by ~4ms.
jordan: 4ms tail likely from slightly higher allocation overhead when forcing slab path — need to measure kernel selection overhead.

kevin: profiling output (perf snippets):
```
GPU mem occupied: -6% overall
alloc/free syscalls: +11%
kernel select hotpath: +2.4% CPU
compaction CPU: -48%
latency tail: +3.9ms (95p)
```

sasha: tradeoff seems promising: fewer OOMs, better overall memory, acceptable tail.
maria: long-term we should: improve slab packing (coalescing strategy), add a lightweight per-stream freelist to satisfy bursty small allocs, and optimize compaction to avoid global pauses.

jordan: also worth exploring adaptive workspace headroom based on recent reuse rate: when reuse falls below X, raise WS reserve to prevent cascade OOMs.
tara: agree. propose rollout plan:
- short term: keep slab-force canary, monitor cost and 99p latency
- medium: land per-stream freelist + compact incremental
- long: revisit kernel routing heuristics to avoid forcing chunk path for bursty patterns

kevin: FYI perf-bot traces here: https://perf.internal/trace/2156784321/ghost-blocks
perf-bot: trace uploaded — flamegraphs + allocation timeline available.

sasha: one more wrinkle — dedicated customers on A-tier saw a different pattern: chunk path was originally chosen to lower latency at the cost of some fragmentation. for them, forcing slab increased p95 beyond SLA. we need policy: route by customer tier.
maria: simple policy rule: if tier==A and p95_target<40ms -> prefer chunk (but enable aggressive background compaction); else prefer slab.

jordan: we should also add a regression test in CI that simulates high small-block churn and asserts no spike in compaction_count and OOM under baseline memory.
tara: adding to backlog. i'll open a ticket for CI harness + canary dashboard alerts for compaction_count > 5/min.

sasha: thanks all. next sync after 24h of canary data. @deploy-bot please keep canary pinned and roll back automatically if OOM rate > 1%.
deploy-bot: pinned canary, alert rule created: OOM_rate > 1% -> rollback. :white_check_mark:
